brief.scope: Review watchdog at this dev snapshot for bounded efficiency and reporting-correctness improvements. Read ops/conductor/watchdog-lever.md, implementation, and existing watchdog tests. Assess tick cost as history grows, forge request/exit semantics, live-job responsiveness and signal/noise. Preserve declared observations; distinguish implementation fixes from contract changes requiring owner ratification. Source review only: no edits, test suites, live forge/store reads or new probes. Return required JSON envelope with actionable findings, source-evidence commands and concrete impact; mark behavior not executed. Do not build a replacement monitor or widen the Python incumbent. If something outside these questions changes the verdict, report it. If running long, return an honest bounded report.

findings.claim: Tick cost as history grows: each tick walks every job directory and re-reads record.json, state.json, in/plan.md, and the full held log files, including records already in startup_closed whose deviation lines already printed; Watch.__init__ also calls entries(), so the first tick is two full walks. The contract already prints each line once per record, so skipping a closed record after its first successful deviation scan is an implementation fix, not a contract change. Impact: IO and parse cost grow with store history and log size, and that work sits on the same serial path as live-job classification. Not executed: no planted-store timing and no live store read.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; s=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); i=s.index('self.scan_deviations(e)'); j=s.index('if e.kind == \"closed\":', i); assert i<j; assert 'held_text(entry, (\"stdout\", \"stderr\", \"launcher.log\"))' in s; assert 'entries(args.store' in s[s.index('class Watch'):s.index('def once')]; print(s[:i].count(chr(10))+1, s[:j].count(chr(10))+1)"

findings.claim: Forge request/exit semantics: forge() calls gh pr list --base <trunk> --state open with no --limit, then gh pr checks once per listed PR, each through run() with a 90s timeout whose TimeoutExpired, missing binary, and non-zero exit all become None with stderr discarded. Sibling onboard-lever.md names a silent first page as a false total and onboard.py passes --limit 200; branches.py passes --limit 1000; ci.py uses a 30s timeout and names timeout as gh-error. Impact: heartbeat open-PR counts and ci fail/cancel lines silently omit PRs past gh's first page, and one hung checks call holds the tick for 90s with only heartbeat unreachable as the exit signal. Implementation: pass an explicit --limit, bound timeout, and let a timeout surface as the existing watchdog error line. Switching away from gh pr checks per PR would be a contract change requiring owner ratification. Not executed: gh was not invoked.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); assert '--limit' not in w and 'timeout=90' in w and '\"pr\", \"list\"' in w and '\"pr\", \"checks\"' in w; assert 'return result.stdout if result.returncode == 0 else None' in w; ob=Path('ops/conductor/onboard-lever.md').read_text(); assert 'silent first page' in ob and 'false total' in ob; print('no --limit; timeout=90; failures->None; onboard names silent first page as a false total')"

findings.claim: Live-job responsiveness: loop() always sleeps the full --tick after run_tick returns, and run_tick runs forge() on the same serial path as harness-gone, long, and settling classification, so the time between live observations is work plus tick, not the tick advertised on the armed line. A record with no state.json pid returns harness_alive() None and is appended to running rather than gone. Impact: a slow or hung forge delays detection of a dead harness past the default 300s cadence; a launched record that never gained a pid is counted running until the long fallback. Implementation: remainder-sleep so --tick is the period; treat a missing pid as not alive. Two-tick settling (ten minutes at the default tick) is declared in the contract and is not this finding. Not executed: the loop was not run.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); loop=w[w.index('def loop'):w.index('def parse_args')]; rt=w[w.index('def run_tick'):w.index('def launcher_count')]; ha=w[w.index('def harness_alive'):w.index('def entries')]; assert 'time.sleep(self.args.tick)' in loop and 'self.forge()' in rt and 'time.sleep' not in rt and 'return None' in ha; print('full-tick sleep after run_tick; forge inside run_tick; missing pid -> None')"

findings.claim: Signal/noise: launcher_count uses pgrep -fc with regex ^python3 .*launch.py (anchored at the word python3) while dispatch.sh execs argv0=$LAUNCHER_PIN (shebang #!/usr/bin/env python3) and ladder.py uses sys.executable. The existing tests never pin that regex. Impact: the count reads 0 on the healthy dispatch path, so launchers fewer than running records fires as R changes and cannot be told from a real dead-launcher case. Implementation: match the argv the wrapper actually execs. Putting the launcher pid on the record is declared out of scope (contract heuristic / fix-scope item 32) and is not required. Not executed: pgrep was not run against live processes.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); d=Path('ops/conductor/tools/dispatch.sh').read_text(); l0=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py').read_text().splitlines()[0]; t=Path('ops/conductor/tests/test_watchdog.py').read_text(); lc=w[w.index('def launcher_count'):w.index('def forge')]; assert 'pgrep' in lc and '-fc' in lc and 'python3' in lc; assert 'LAUNCHER_PIN' in d and 'argv=' in d; assert l0=='#!/usr/bin/env python3'; assert 'pgrep' not in t; print([ln.strip() for ln in lc.splitlines() if '-fc' in ln][0]); print('dispatch argv0 LAUNCHER_PIN; shebang', l0)"

findings.claim: Signal/noise: scan_deviations reads held files named stdout, stderr, and launcher.log, but the launcher contract names raw.out as the harness stdout byte-for-byte and launch.py writes that path; watchdog.py never mentions raw.out. Impact: deviation errors that exist only in harness stdout (the held-files path, when the envelope note does not already say errored) never fire — a false negative — while the named stdout file is usually absent. Implementation: treat raw.out as the held stdout (keep stdout if present). Renaming the lever's word stdout to raw.out is a contract wording change for the owner; aliasing in the reader is not. Not executed: no planted job directory was scanned.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); c=Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md').read_text(); assert 'raw.out' not in w and '\"stdout\"' in w and 'raw.out' in c; print('watchdog reads stdout; launcher writes raw.out')"

findings.claim: Live-job responsiveness: entries() catches OSError from store.iterdir and returns an empty list, so a store that becomes unreadable after arming produces heartbeat running=none with no watchdog error line. The contract names the watchdog error line for a tick exception and for unreadable record.json or state.json; a store-level read failure is swallowed instead. Impact: live jobs vanish from the report without an error. Implementation: raise or print the existing error line. Not executed.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; w=Path('ops/conductor/tools/watchdog.py').read_text(); fn=w[w.index('def entries'):w.index('def text_values')]; assert 'except OSError:' in fn and 'return out' in fn; print(fn[fn.index('except OSError:'):fn.index('for d in dirs')])"
